rationale_overall: This week's pool was dominated by noise irrelevant to actionable US-listed wave exposure: geopolitical/military reporting (Russia-Ukraine drone and missile strikes, Gaza rocket fire, India-Pakistan tactical missile tests, Israel exercises) with no investable equity angle; foreign or state-run satellite launches (Pakistan/China remote-sensing satellite, China's own internet-satellite launch, India-NASA NISAR) with no US-listed line; private-company catalysts with no public ticker (SpaceX Starlink/Crew-11 missions, Holtec's Palisades Michigan nuclear restart, York Space Systems' BARD launch, Cascade's $59M funding round); a Boeing (BA) fighter-jet labor dispute that is a risk signal rather than a clean buildup catalyst; a Samsung earnings miss in AI chips; and generic Beijing robotics-conference coverage with no specific vehicle named. Two items brushed against genuine theses -- BlackSky's (BKSY) incremental Navy satellite-link contract phase, and Tesla/Samsung's $16.5B AI-chip fab deal in Texas -- but neither rises to a 'clearly stronger rising wave vehicle' bar sufficient to displace an existing mega-cap AI holding on a single week's headline, especially against a weekly cadence that should mostly hold. No swap is warranted; watchlist unchanged this period.
